subject: SIG: artifact provenance & redaction guidance for Longview RFI
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@longview.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Longview Procurement <procurement@longview.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire - artifact provenance / redaction asks

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this RFI — Longview is working through the vendor SIG and has specific asks around evidence we can accept for control mapping. A few clarifying points from our security team: 

1) Provenance: we need an artifact manifest that shows where each piece of evidence came from (system, export time, and the Redwood product component). For example: audit logs exported from the private control plane, KMS rotation records, and runtime telemetry from inference nodes.

2) Redaction rules: we need to understand how you can remove or obfuscate customer PII and customer-provided prompt content from artifacts prior to delivery. Please provide a deterministic redaction approach (so Longview can validate) and any proof you retain to show integrity of the artifact after redaction.

3) Retention windows: what retention windows apply to raw telemetry vs. curated evidence that we will receive for SOC 2/ISO requests? We have internal policies that require retaining some items for 1+ year.

4) Chain of custody: any timestamps, signing, or hashes you can include to show the evidence hasn't been tampered with while in transit.

Attached is our SIG excerpt and the sections where we expect artifact-level answers. Can you confirm what you can provide and the expected lead time?

Thanks,
Anjali Rao
Security Program Manager
Longview Systems

Attachment: Longview_SIG_Questions_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

I'll draft the reply to Anjali after we align.

- Grace

Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG questionnaire - artifact provenance / redaction asks

Grace — quick technical notes. We can deliver everything they're asking for with the following specifics: 

1) Artifact manifest: we will produce a CSV with columns: control_id, artifact_name, component, export_timestamp_utc, sha256_hex, redaction_applied (yes/no), redaction_spec_version, signed_by (service-account). We sign the manifest with a long-lived Redwood KMS key and include the KMS key id in the manifest.

2) Redaction pipeline: for artifacts that contain request-level data (traces, telemetry snippets) we will:
   - Remove full request payloads; retain only deterministic metadata (request_id, model_id, latency_ms, status_code).
   - Replace any string fields flagged as PII/user-provided content with HMAC-SHA256(<field_value>, customer_salt_v1). The salt is generated per-customer and stored in our secrets store; we will include the salt_id (not the salt itself) in the manifest so Longview can reproduce hashing if they have a pre-shared verification key.
   - For binary artifacts (screenshots, attachments) we will either not export or provide a redacted rendering with overlays.

3) Integrity/chain-of-custody: each artifact exported will be accompanied by a sha256 digest. The manifest is signed via KMS and the signature included. We can also provide a per-export timestamped envelope signed with an ephemeral key and notarized by our internal signing service (signature header in the manifest).

4) Retention windows (recommended defaults):
   - Raw runtime traces (unredacted): retained for 30 days by default; can extend to 180 days with a documented business case.
   - Curated export bundles and manifests (what we deliver for compliance): retained for 3 years in our archives (immutable store) unless customer requests deletion earlier.
   - KMS rotation records and key provenance audit trails: retained for 7 years.

Edge cases: Private deployments (customer-managed control plane) — we can provide instructions and tooling (export scripts) for customers to produce the same manifest locally; in that case we provide the redaction spec and verification tooling but do not extract their raw logs.

I'll attach a sample manifest template and a one-page redaction spec. Jordan, can you confirm the signature/envelope flow and whether we should surface an additional HSM-attested signing option for enterprise customers?

—Karthik
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG: artifact provenance & redaction guidance for Longview RFI

Hi Anjali — thanks for the clear asks and the SIG excerpt. We can provide a compliance-ready export bundle and a signed manifest that maps evidence to SIG control IDs. Summary below and next steps.

What we will deliver:
- Artifact manifest CSV (signed): control_id -> artifact filename -> component origin -> export timestamp (UTC) -> SHA256 digest -> redaction flag -> signing metadata.
- Redaction spec v1.0: deterministic HMAC-based obfuscation for user content, field-level redaction rules, and a list of fields we will never export (full prompt text, raw customer-uploaded files).
- Sample export bundle: one example package with a redacted trace, the signed manifest, and verification instructions.
- Retention commitments: curated export bundles and manifests retained 3 years; KMS rotation trails retained 7 years; raw, unredacted traces kept 30 days by default (we can extend on request).

Chain-of-custody & verification:
- Each manifest is signed with Redwood's KMS key (key id included). We will provide the SHA256 digests for all artifacts. For enterprise customers we can offer an HSM-attested signing option (requires addendum).

Private deployment note:
- If Longview uses Redwood Private / customer-managed control plane, we will provide the export tooling and redaction spec so your team can run exports locally and produce an identical manifest format. Redwood engineering support is available for a hands-on session.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm you are accepting the redaction approach (HMAC with salt_id) and the proposed retention windows.
2) If yes, we will deliver the draft manifest + redaction spec within 3 business days and a sample bundle within 7 business days.
3) Offer: 30-minute technical validation call — we are available Thu/Fri this week.

Thanks — we'll attach the manifest template and redaction spec to a shared Drive (link below) once the internal review is done.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
